cues.text: Hey everybody, this is Ralphie boy here.
Today I just want to talk briefly about
my process on pre-grading. I'm just to
give you a couple couple of things that
I've learned grading cards. So, let's
talk about this. I created checklist. I
do. I keep my checklist beside the area
where I do a lot of my pre-grading and
it's a pretty simple checklist, right?
It says centering, corners, edges,
surface and repeat on the back. And I
make sure I hit all those before I would
ever consider putting any card into my
box to send off to PSA. So, let's talk a
little bit. Get yourself a centering
tool. I use them 60/40 on the front. You
know, you need that at the bare minimum.
If I see a card and I use my centering
tool and it comes out 60/40, it has to
be perfect everywhere else because I
think with a 60/40 at the bare minimum,
you are really rolling the dice. You
really want to see your centering a
little bit better than that to be safe,
okay? Well, on the back it says 90/10. I
don't believe it. I've sent cards in
with a 90/10 on the back and they've not
received a 10. So, I would make sure my
back is better centered than what they
are telling you is the minimum
requirements. That's just me. You be
you, all right? Corners, any frayed
corners, any white at all, even a little
bit that I can see naked eye, I will not
send that card in. You will not get the
10. Corners are a big big part of what
PSA looks at. We all forget about edges.
If I'm going to pick one thing that I
forget about every time I send in not
every time, but actually when I send
cards in, it's edges, all right? So,
make sure you take the time to check
that off your list. Look for any kind of
nick along these frames, especially if
the frame of your card is a different
color than white. You know, you're
really going to see that. It's really
going to show up. So, just be careful
that you're not seeing that and again,
do it on the back, right? And the big
thing, I mean, the one thing that can
really drop your card multiple grades is
surface.
I do not send in any cards that have a
print line on the on the front. A single
faint print line is a disqualification
for me. I do not send that card in. I
have sent cards in with print lines on
the back, however, and they have
received tens.
However, it's got to be it's got to be,
you know, not a lot of them and it's got
to be really hard to see with the naked
eye. If you have multiple print lines
coming across a colored area on the back
of your card, you are more than likely
not going to get the 10. At least that's
what my have experienced in my days
grading cards. All right, so kind of
keep that in mind as well. Any pop marks
that I get, if there is one pop mark on
certain cards, and those certain cards
are the ones that are, you know, the
real shiny ones, right? The Optic Rated
Rookies, the Mosaic, um some of these
other ones that have that kind of a
sheen to it. If I have one pop mark
that's not in a bad spot that my eyes
don't go directly to when I look at that
card, well then I'll send that card in
because I've gotten 10s that way. I've
also gotten 9s, but I've gotten 10s. But
other than that, if I have pop marks on
the card that my eyes see with the naked
eye, I I'm not sending it in. It's an
automatic 9. Could be even worse if you
miss something else, okay? So, again, go
through your checklist, centering,
corners, edges, surface, repeat on the
back, use your centering tool, use your
magnifying glass cuz who knows if PSA is
using these at all. I'm sure if they
find something on your card they don't
like, uh they're going to look at it.
So, go ahead and do use those tools.
Make sure you get those. I hope this was
helpful. I'm trying to keep it simple
for you. Um thanks for watching and take
care.
